rules.rule: Niva Bupa's migration article (published 19 Jun 2023, modified 1 Sep 2026) says not to let the old policy lapse while waiting for confirmation, because hospitals will not treat an application in progress as proof of cover. The same page still gives an out-of-date '45 to 60 days' window for porting.
rules.exact_text: Do not let the old policy lapse while waiting for confirmation on the new one. A gap in coverage leaves you unprotected, and hospitals will not treat an application in progress as proof of cover.
rules.effective_from: Article dated 2023-06-19, modified 2026-09-01
rules.implication_for_switcher: Keep the old policy active until the new insurer has issued the policy. This is an insurer blog and is written about migration. The same page also gives an out-of-date 45-to-60-day porting window.

rules.rule: On porting, credits for sum insured, NCB, specific waiting periods, PED waiting period and moratorium may be transferred.
rules.exact_text: 24.6. The policyholder is entitled to transfer the credits gained to the extent of the Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus, specific waiting periods, waiting period for pre-existing disease, Moratorium period etc. from the policy of Existing Insurer to the new policy issued by the Acquiring Insurer.
rules.effective_from: 2024-09-05 (same wording in Health MC 29-05-2024 para 12(d))
rules.implication_for_switcher: You get credit for the time already served. You do not get a copy of the old policy. If the new policy has longer waiting periods, you still serve the rest. The new insurer's own features, limits and exclusions apply.

rules.rule: Niva Bupa ReAssure 2.0 has a 36-month PED wait (Excl01) and a 24-month listed-conditions wait (Excl02). Each is reduced by prior continuous coverage without a break, and each applies afresh to any sum-insured increase.
rules.exact_text: a. Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy. b. In case of enhancement of Sum Insured the exclusion shall apply afresh to the extent of Sum Insured increase. c. If the Insured Person is continuously covered without any break as defined under the portability norms of the extant IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, ... then waiting period for the same would be reduced to the extent of prior coverage.
rules.effective_from: UIN NBHHLIP27054V032627 (Excl01), as downloaded 2026-10-07
rules.implication_for_switcher: Compare the old and new waiting periods side by side. A move from a 2-year to a 3-year pre-existing disease wait after 2 years of cover leaves about 1 more year uncovered for those conditions.

rules.rule: Credits carry over to the extent of the previous sum insured and accrued No Claim Bonus. PPHI MC 24.6 lists both SI and NCB, and insurer wordings such as HDFC ERGO credit previous SI plus accrued cumulative bonus. Any SI above that is an enhancement. Its moratorium runs afresh for 60 months on the enhanced limits only (Sch III cl.8). Waiting periods apply afresh to the enhanced portion (CIS template and insurer wordings), and the increase may be underwritten.
rules.exact_text: The moratorium would be applicable for the sums insured of the first policy. Wherever, the sum insured is enhanced, completion of sixty continuous months would be applicable from the date of enhancement of sums insured only on the enhanced limits.
rules.effective_from: 2024-04-01 (Schedule III cl. 8; portability 'to the extent of the sum insured' in cl. 10.2)
rules.implication_for_switcher: A larger cover at the new insurer is not fully usable from day one. The added amount is new cover with fresh waits and can be contested for non-disclosure for 5 years. The increase is also underwritten.

rules.rule: After 60 months of continuous coverage, no policy or claim can be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except for established fraud. Credits accrued under ported and migrated policies count toward the 60 months.
rules.exact_text: 13) Policy/Claim cannot be contested: No policy and claim of health insurance shall be contestable on any grounds of non-disclosure and/or misrepresentation except for established fraud, after the completion of the Moratorium Period, i.e. 60 months of continuous coverage. Note: The accrued credits gained under the ported and migrated policies shall be counted for the purpose of calculating the Moratorium period.
rules.effective_from: 2024-05-29 (also Products Regs Sch. III cl. 8, from 2024-04-01)
rules.implication_for_switcher: Switching does not restart the 5-year clock on the sum insured you carry over. It does restart for any increase. The porting proposal is still a new declaration, and if you are under 5 years in total it can be used against you.

rules.rule: Niva Bupa: PED cover after 36 months requires the PED to have been declared and accepted. Misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact voids the policy and forfeits the premium.
rules.exact_text: d. Coverage under the Policy after the expiry of 36 months for any Pre-existing Disease is subject to the same being declared at the time of application and accepted by Us. ... 6.1.14. Disclosure of Information: The Policy shall be void and all premium paid thereon shall be forfeited to the Company in the event of misrepresentation, mis-description or non-disclosure of any material fact by the policyholder.
rules.effective_from: UIN NBHHLIP27054V032627, as downloaded 2026-10-07
rules.implication_for_switcher: The porting proposal form is a fresh declaration. Hiding a condition to avoid a loading or a rejection can leave that condition uncovered permanently, or void the policy until the moratorium is complete. The new insurer also sees your claim history through IIB.

rules.rule: Star Comprehensive (Multiple Policies condition): the policyholder is expected to disclose all health policies covering the proposed lives. For non-disclosure of previous policies, or for multiple policies exceeding the product's maximum sum insured, Star may cancel any or all of the policies the policyholder opted for, ab initio, except the first-issued policy.
rules.exact_text: The Policyholder is expected to disclose all the health insurance policies under which the lives proposed for insurance are covered. The company reserves the right to cancel any / all of the policies (except the 1st issued Policy) opted by the Policyholder ab-initio, in case of any non-disclosure of previous policies and / or having multiple policies that exceeds the maximum Sum Insured filed as per the Product.
rules.implication_for_switcher: When switching, list all existing covers on the proposal, including employer group policies and top-ups.

rules.rule: IRDAI texts transfer NCB credit without saying how it is shown or priced. Loyalty, wellness and renewal incentives are optional, insurer-designed features under Sch III 4.2.
rules.exact_text: 4.2 Insurers may devise mechanism(s) or incentive(s) to reward policyholders for early entry, continued renewals, favourable claims experience, preventive and wellness habits and disclose upfront such mechanism or incentives in the prospectus and the policy document.
rules.effective_from: 2024-04-01 (Schedule III cl. 4.2)
rules.implication_for_switcher: Expect to lose product-specific perks such as wellness discounts (e.g. Niva Bupa 'Live Healthy' up to 30%), loyalty or early-entry pricing, and possibly carried-forward unused cover (e.g. Niva Bupa 'Booster+' up to 3/5/10x). The transfer list covers sum insured, no-claim bonus, waiting periods and moratorium only. Whether a given bonus counts as 'No Claim Bonus' for porting is decided case by case, so get it in writing.

rules.rule: Niva Bupa ReAssure 2.0 'Lock the Clock': the premium is charged at the age at entry when you buy the policy, until a claim is paid. After a claim it follows current age slabs.
rules.exact_text: 4.7.2. Lock the Clock: Your age is locked at entry when you buy the policy, till a claim is paid. E.g. if you buy the policy at 25 years, you will keep paying the premium applicable for a 25 year old at each renewal, till a claim is paid in the policy. Post the claim is paid, the premium charged will be as per your current age and will continue to change as per the age slabs at each renewal.
rules.effective_from: UIN NBHHLIP27054V032627, as downloaded 2026-10-07
rules.implication_for_switcher: This is an inference; the wording has no portability-specific clause. Leaving a Lock-the-Clock policy likely means losing the frozen-age premium. Porting into one likely locks your age at the time of porting, not your original entry age with the old insurer.

rules.rule: Migration means moving to another product of the same insurer, keeping credits to the extent of the previous SI and benefits. The insurer may underwrite only if the insured has not been continuously covered for 36 months.
rules.exact_text: 10.1 General insurers and health insurers offering indemnity based health insurance policy except Personal Accident and Travel Policies, shall provide an option of migration to an alternative health insurance product to the extent of the sum insured and the benefits available in the previous policy. The insurer may underwrite the proposal in case of migration, if the insured is not continuously covered for 36 months.
rules.implication_for_switcher: If the problem is the plan rather than the insurer, migrating after 36 months of continuous cover avoids the re-underwriting risk that porting carries.

rules.rule: Mandatory portability (Sch III 10.2) covers only indemnity health policies of general and health insurers, excluding personal accident and travel. Life insurers, which may offer only benefit-based health products, 'may allow portability, wherever possible, as per the policy terms'.
rules.exact_text: 10.3 Life insurers may allow portability, wherever possible, as per the policy terms.
rules.implication_for_switcher: Fixed-benefit covers such as critical-illness or hospital-cash plans, especially from life insurers, may have no porting right at all. The app should flag the policy type before suggesting a switch.

rules.rule: The acquiring insurer provides the Portability Form, which authorises it to obtain policy and claim data. The policyholder submits it with the proposal form.
rules.exact_text: 24.3. The acquiring insurer shall furnish to the policyholder, the Portability Form authorizing it to obtain policy and claim related information from the existing insurer. The policyholder shall fill in the portability form along with proposal form and submit the same to the acquiring insurer.
rules.implication_for_switcher: You need two forms, the proposal form and the portability form, both from the new insurer.

rules.rule: SBI General's porting document list: a duly filled and signed proposal form, a duly filled and signed portability form, all previous years' policy copies, and claim history (if any) for those policies with the claim documents. The same PDF states the 30-to-60-day window.
rules.exact_text: List of documents • Duly filled & signed Proposal form, • Duly filled & signed Portability form, • All Previous Year policy copies, • Claim history (if any) for all the Previous Year policies along with Claim documents
rules.effective_from: As downloaded 2026-10-07 (undated PDF; it states the 30-to-60-day window)
rules.implication_for_switcher: Before you start, gather every year's policy schedule (continuity is proved year by year) and the paperwork for any past claim.

rules.rule: Star Health asks for the proposal and portability forms, copies of the previous policies, and pre-insurance medical reports where applicable. Medical examination is done at Star's cost.
rules.exact_text: Proposal Form and Portability form to be duly filled, signed and submitted along with the following documents, Policy copies of the previous insurance. Pre Insurance medical examination reports, wherever, applicable. Medical examination will be done at our cost.
rules.effective_from: As accessed 2026-10-07
rules.implication_for_switcher: Expect possible medical tests, which take time. Book them early within the 30-to-60-day window.

rules.rule: Neither insurer may charge the policyholder for porting in or out. During the port-in year the acquiring insurer may not pay commission or incentive to its employees, its distribution channel, or the channel's employees on port-in policies.
rules.exact_text: 24.7. On the port-in policies during the port-in year, acquiring insurer shall not pay any commission or incentive to its own employees or distribution channel or employees of the distribution channel. No charges shall be levied on the policyholder for porting-in or porting-out.
rules.implication_for_switcher: Refuse any 'porting fee'. My inference: agents earn nothing on a port in year one, so be wary if one suggests a fresh policy instead. A fresh policy throws away your waiting-period and moratorium credits.

rules.rule: Star Comprehensive: free look applies to new individual policies, not on renewals or when porting or migrating.
rules.exact_text: Free Look Period: The Free Look Period shall be applicable on new individual health insurance policies and not on renewals or at the time of porting/migrating the policy.
rules.implication_for_switcher: With some insurers you cannot undo a port by free-look cancellation once the policy is issued. Read the offer, including any loadings or exclusions, before you pay. This varies by insurer: Niva Bupa's wording excludes only renewals, and IRDAI's master circulars do not mention porting.
